what: The pinned Blaze bootstrap rejected a Cargo-compatible lockfile as a formatting change. Its exact resolver output reordered five unused patch entries, which then made Cargo --locked refuse the same dependency graph.
cost: Repeated bootstrap failures, followed by a partial-library job refusing to start after adopting the pinned resolver's output.
cause: Pinned Blaze preserves patch declaration order when writing unused patches; Cargo writes those entries alphabetically.
whys: the manifest's patch table was not sorted
the two builders serialize the unused subset differently despite agreeing on every package and dependency edge
the bootstrap's format-only refusal did not print the differing lines
class: a shared lockfile has incompatible canonical orders across builders
prevention: Keep all patch declarations sorted, so every unused subset has the same order for both builders. The locked build flags and independent native library controls remain enabled.
fix: Sorted all 13 patch declarations without changing parsed manifest values. Restored the exact Cargo.lock that passed 117 native tests. A fail-closed diagnostic captures the pinned resolver's proposed files and diff in an isolated snapshot.
state: ordering fix applied; paired CI verification pending
